heuristic_statement: An audit finding of present corrective work is legitimate if and only if a requirement originated from an authentic user instruction or specification baseline, has not undergone complete subsequent supersession, and remains missing, partially implemented, unenforced, or incorrectly represented in today's deterministic executable runtime, workflows, or active configuration. Normative implementation reality is established solely by executable code and deterministic execution paths—not by specification prose, filenames, or self-reported completions. Historical evidence must be evaluated through a strict three-tier epistemic chain: verified historical facts (exact commits, diffs, persisted runtime artifacts) -> explicit semantic interpretations (intent, failure cause, requirement scope) -> normative truth decisions (surviving status, supersession classification, active defects).
decomposition_rationale: To prevent quota exhaustion and ensure deterministic, sequential evaluation within the 250,000-byte context ceiling, the audit is divided into 28 focused subquestions across five distinct operational domains: (1) Current Executable Machine (inspecting actual Node.js code, Action workflows, active rulebooks, and configuration); (2) Stated Specifications and Evaluation Contracts (evaluating Agents.md, Step 3 heuristics, and retired evaluation standards); (3) Historical Lineage and Mutation Provenance (tracing Git commit history, patch logs, and dependency transitions); (4) Nonce Execution Evidence (dissecting individual run logs, error transitions, schema rejections, and test suites across all 16 nonce runs); and (5) Supersession Analysis, Completeness Reconciliation, and Defect Synthesis (mapping requirement lifecycles from origin to current status, cross-reconciling subquestion outputs, and cataloging surviving defects).
